newsitem.title: USA: Croatian diplomat says Tudjman performing duties.
newsitem.headline: Croatian diplomat says Tudjman performing duties.

text.p: Croatian President Franjo Tudjman, under treatment at a Washington hospital, was feeling well and was working, a diplomat at Croatia's embassy said on Sunday.
"He feels well. He's performing his duties," the Croatian diplomat said in a brief telephone interview.
U.S. officials said late last week that Tudjman was seriously ill and was being treated at Walter Reed Hospital for stomach cancer.

Croatian government officials, apparently anxious to discourage speculation about the 74-year-old president's health, have avoided any mention of cancer and described his illness as a "digestion problem."
On Saturday, one of Tudjman's doctors confirmed to Croatian state television by telephone from Washington that Tudjman was at Walter Reed and said he was still able to discharge his duties.
Hematologist Branimir Jaksic said that since Tudjman began receiving therapy, "the disorders have been subsiding." He said Tudjman's disorder was diagnosed as having been caused by a stomach ulcer.
Jasic said Tudjman would soon be returning to Croatia.
